references.text: The parallel passage in the Sermon on the Mount where Jesus uses the same image of the eye as the lamp of the body. [ref:Matt 6:22-23|Matthew 6:22-23] contains almost identical wording: "The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light. But if your eye is bad, your whole body will be in darkness."

The preceding verse [ref:Luk 11:33|Luke 11:33] speaks of the lamp placed on a stand so that those who enter may see the light – the context leading directly into the image of the eye as the lamp of the body.

The following exhortation in [ref:Luk 11:35-36|Luke 11:35-36] expands on this image further: "See to it that the light within you is not darkness!" and describes the body as completely illuminated when the lamp shines upon you with its radiance.

[ref:Ordsp 4:18-19|Proverbs 4:18-19] contrasts the path of the righteous, which is like the shining morning light, with the way of the wicked, which is like darkness – they do not know what they stumble over. The same contrast between light and darkness as in Luke 11:34.
[ref:Ordsp 20:27|Proverbs 20:27] says that "the human spirit is the Lord's lamp", a parallel to the idea that an inner lamp illuminates the person.

Paul prays that "the eyes of your heart may be enlightened" in [ref:Ef 1:18|Ephesians 1:18], reflecting the connection between spiritual sight and inner light, just as Jesus speaks of the eye as the lamp of the body.
[ref:2 Pet 1:19|2 Peter 1:19] speaks of the prophetic word as a lamp shining in a dark place – a related image where light represents spiritual insight and clarity.
[ref:1 Joh 2:11|1 John 2:11] describes the one who hates their brother as someone walking in darkness, blinded by darkness – a parallel to how an "evil" eye makes the whole body dark.

The expression "evil eye" (πονηρός ὀφθαλμός) is also used in [ref:Matt 20:15|Matthew 20:15], where it means envy or greed. This can shed light on what Jesus means by an "evil eye" in contrast to the "healthy" (ἁπλοῦς, which can also mean 'generous') eye.

[ref:Jes 60:1-2|Isaiah 60:1-2] speaks of the Lord's glory shining upon the people while darkness covers the earth – a prophetic contrast between light and darkness that forms the background for Jesus' teaching about light and darkness in humanity.
